title: Reciprocal Skin Effect from Internal Rotation
authors: Kin Hung Fung, C. T. Chan
abstract: We present a class of lattices in which an internal rotation---a conserved compact angular momentum in each unit cell---turns reciprocal couplings into a non-Hermitian skin effect. In each conserved channel, the rotation character makes the left- and right-going amplitudes unequal, so the channel localizes directionally while the full Hamiltonian remains reciprocal, with conjugate channels pinned to opposite boundaries. Every channel is exactly solvable and carries an integer point-gap winding: under exact channel conservation, the phases form $\Z^{q}$, with one integer per conjugate channel pair, $q$ unbounded across multiplets, and $q=j+\tfrac{1}{2}$ for half-integer spin $j$ in the symplectic class AII$^{\dagger}$. Mixing conjugate channels collapses the grading to a critical, scale-free skin effect, with only the odd AII$^{\dagger}$ $\Z_{2}$ parity surviving. A cyclic three-site lattice and a passive lossy resonator array realize the effect.
summary: This work introduces the 'reciprocal skin effect' in lattice models by incorporating an internal conserved angular momentum (internal rotation). This mechanism generates a rich, graded topological invariant ($\mathbb{Z}_q$) that dictates directional localization while maintaining overall Hamiltonian reciprocity. The findings provide a powerful theoretical tool for designing quantum systems with controlled, symmetry-protected transport properties.
main_problem: To construct a general mechanism where an internal, conserved compact angular momentum converts standard lattice couplings into a reciprocal non-Hermitian skin effect.
main_result: The system exhibits a graded topological invariant ($\mathbb{Z}_q$) protected by the internal rotation, leading to directional localization that is balanced between opposite boundaries (reciprocal skin effect).
method: Theoretical analysis of lattice Hamiltonians involving rotational couplings, utilizing concepts from non-Hermitian topology and spectral theory.
model_or_system: A class of lattices featuring an 'internal rotation'—a conserved compact angular momentum in each unit cell. The model is analyzed using a rotor chain Hamiltonian structure $H\psi = h_0(Jz) \psi + T_R \psi_{n+1} + T_L \psi_{n-1}$.
key_observables: Directional Imbalance Generator ($g_m$), Integer Grading ($\mathbb{Z}_q$) winding numbers, and the skin localization length ($\xi_m$).
important_parameters: The rotational parameter $\alpha$, spin quantum number $j$ (integer or half-integer), and coupling strengths ($t_0, t_1$).
main_assumptions: The existence of a multi-mode internal space carrying a nontrivial rotation representation and the conservation of angular momentum $J_z$.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the general mechanism via internal rotation leading to directional imbalance, derives the topological invariants ($\mathbb{Z}_q$), analyzes the behavior across different spin classes (integer vs. half-integer), and confirms realizations using specific lattices like the cyclic three-site model or passive lossy resonators.
why_interesting: The concept of a 'reciprocal skin effect' protected by internal symmetry is a sophisticated extension of standard non-Hermitian physics, providing new topological invariants ($\mathbb{Z}_q$) beyond simple $\mathbb{Z}_2$ indices. This framework could apply to engineered quantum metamaterials or optical lattices.
